title: Could a volcano change the world's climate?
sources: USGS Volcano Hazards Program Climate Effects

lines.text: Can a single catastrophic volcanic eruption actually plunge the entire planet into an icy volcanic winter?
History has proven that the answer is an undeniable yes.
lines.caps: History proves that the *answer | is an undeniable *yes!

lines.text: When Indonesia's Mount Tambora erupted in eighteen fifteen, it blasted sixty million tons of sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere.
lines.caps: Blasted 60 million tons of *sulfur | high into the *stratosphere

lines.text: The sulfur reacted with water vapor to form a shimmering global blanket of sulfate aerosol droplets.
lines.caps: Formed a global *veil of aerosols | reflecting solar *radiation

lines.text: This volcanic veil reflected incoming sunlight back into space, cooling global temperatures for three straight years.
Eighteen sixteen became known as the 'Year Without a Summer', with blizzards hitting New England in July.
lines.caps: Snow fell in *New England | in the middle of *July

lines.text: Massive volcanic eruptions hold the raw power to rewrite global climate overnight.
lines.caps: Volcanoes have the *raw power | to rewrite Earth's *climate!
